topic: model efficiency; compression; quantization; parameter-efficient adaptation; LLM serving
status: cross-period synthesis from six fixed-frame random full texts; external replication and global novelty unresolved
claim: The six uniformly frame-sampled model-efficiency papers do not support a single efficiency claim. They optimize different resource axes and expose different counterconditions: tensor compression quality depends on decomposition (at 10% ResNet32/CIFAR10 parameters TNN-mTK trails its conventional baseline); INT7 EasyQuant retains ImageNet ResNet50 classification closely but loses 3.25 mAP points on MobileNet-SSD/VOC2007 while reducing measured latency on two ARM boards; LoRA cuts per-task trainable state but still requires the shared base model and its forward pass; Inheritune reduces training steps for a smaller model by inheriting a larger pretrained model's weights; MoE-Lens accelerates offline batch throughput on a specific CPU/A40 server with workload-dependent maxima; and 3-bit LLM quantization retention varies sharply with algorithm, model scale, and task. The better-supported common conclusion is that cost and quality must be reported on separate, explicit axes rather than compressed into one “efficient” score.

interpretation: This synthesis joins conceptually related but non-comparable studies: CNN tensor factorization, edge INT7 inference, LLM adaptation, pretrained-model layer inheritance, MoE serving, and weight-only LLM quantization. The figures are not pooled. It is evidence that “efficiency” is under-specified, not a claim that one technique dominates or that every field has the same tradeoff. The 2024 arXiv Inheritune paper's final audited version was published in 2026 and cannot be used as a 2024 result in historical cutoff experiments.
falsifiable_question: On matched model families and tasks, do method rankings change when parameter count, task-specific trainable state, checkpoint storage, training compute, end-to-end latency, device/server energy, and workload throughput are measured separately—and do claimed quality-preserving gains persist on a predeclared task likely to be adverse for each technique?
primary_outcome: For each method report task quality plus training and inference FLOPs/time, peak memory, persistent base and task-specific storage, measured latency/energy on named hardware, throughput under named prompt/generation distributions, and whether the large source checkpoint/pretraining cost is amortized or included.
counterevidence_and_caveats: TNN-mCP at one compression point improves over its matched low-rank baseline; some other tensorized variants do not.
EasyQuant INT7 preserves tested classification scores closely and reports real ARM latency savings; this does not transfer automatically to detection or other accelerators.
LoRA can merge into the base with no extra inference-latency path, but keeps the full shared base model.
Inheritune beats same-width scratch baselines in the reported setup, but inherits weights from a larger pretrained model and does not charge that upstream compute.
MoE-Lens reports a real-server throughput gain, but maxima are workload-specific and the target is offline/batched throughput.
The 2026 quantization study shows some W3 method/model combinations retain capability well and others degrade severely; its retention metric is de-randomized and finite-sample-based.
The Inheritune v4 results are from a 2026 TMLR paper despite 2024 arXiv submission; enforce publication chronology in historical analysis.
Global novelty and independent replication are unconfirmed.
suggested_design: Pre-register a shared evaluation matrix across a compact CNN, a decoder LLM, and an MoE server workload. Compare tensor factorization/pruning, INT8/INT7/4/3-bit methods, LoRA/full fine-tuning, inherited smaller-model initialization, and resource-aware serving only where method-model pairs are valid. Use paired quality datasets; name test-time shift/task groups; charge upstream checkpoint and training cost separately from marginal adaptation; measure actual inference hardware. Report a Pareto frontier per resource axis instead of a single weighted rank, then test whether any method is non-dominated across both quality and total lifecycle cost.
